title: Berkshire Sells 27.5M Bank of America Shares: Should Investors Worry?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Berkshire Hathaway reduced its Bank of America stake by 5.7% in Q3 2026, selling 27.5 million shares and bringing its total reduction to 57.8 million shares since March 2026. While the persistent selling by a major institutional investor could create sentiment concerns, BAC's underlying fundamentals remain solid with expected 8% net interest income growth in 2026 and at least 8% in 2027. The stock trades at a discount valuation but faces headwinds from lower earnings estimate revisions and broader institutional selling pressure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed signals: Berkshire's continued stake reduction creates negative sentiment and potential valuation headwinds, but BAC's fundamentals remain solid with strong NII growth guidance (8% in 2026, 8%+ in 2027), favorable earnings prospects, and attractive valuation (P/TB of 1.78 vs industry 3.15). However, recent earnings estimate revisions lower and 1.2% share price decline in six months offset positive fundamentals.

title: Trust Wins Hearts, Deals Win Carts: SYF Eyes Holiday Shopping Gains?
author: Na
description: Synchrony Financial's survey reveals that 83% of consumers plan holiday shopping with trusted retailers while 75% actively seek the best prices. Interest in rewards programs (66%), installment financing (42%), and store cards (40% considering first-purchase discounts) is growing, presenting opportunities for payment processors. However, increased competition and higher rewards-related expenses could pressure profitability across the industry.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Survey findings show strong consumer interest in rewards redemption (66%), installment financing (42%), and store card adoption (40%), which could drive higher card applications, purchase volumes, and deeper retailer partnerships. The company trades at a favorable valuation (P/E 7.00 vs. industry 13.11) with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

title: Software Safety Institute Launches to Reduce Preventable Harm from Insecure Software
author: Not Specified
description: The Software Safety Institute, a new independent nonprofit, launched on November 9, 2026, to advance research and policy on software safety. Founded by Lauren Zabierek and Bob Lord, the organization aims to shift responsibility for software defects from users to manufacturers through independent research, public education, and policy frameworks. The institute argues that preventable software flaws, particularly memory safety issues known for 30 years, persist due to misaligned incentives rather than technical limitations.

title: 5 Payment Stocks That Earn a Fee Every Time You Swipe
author: Daniel Sparks
description: The article analyzes five payment processing stocks that earn fees on transactions: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, PayPal, and Capital One. Visa and Mastercard trade at premium valuations (~28x earnings) due to their low-risk fee-based models with no lending exposure. PayPal and Capital One trade cheaper (~9-10x earnings) due to higher risks from shrinking margins and credit exposure respectively. American Express falls in between at ~16x earnings. The author recommends Visa and Mastercard as the simplest payment fee plays, with Mastercard having a slight edge due to faster-growing services revenue.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Trading at premium 28x earnings multiple justified by pure fee-based model with no credit risk. Handled 74.2B transactions (up 10% YoY) with 13% revenue growth and 17% EPS growth. Author recommends as top choice for simplest payment fee exposure.

Trading at premium 28x earnings with strong fundamentals. Value-added services revenue jumped 19% and now comprises 41% of net revenue, providing diversification. Author gives it slight edge over Visa due to faster-growing services business.

Trading at moderate 16x earnings, falling between pure networks and lenders. Generates fees from merchants but also carries credit risk from lending operations. Net write-off rate improved to 1.8%, but credit quality remains a key risk factor.

Trading cheaply at ~10x earnings due to significant headwinds. Transaction revenue grew only 3% despite 6% payment volume growth, indicating shrinking margins (1.58% cut down from 1.65%). Author identifies margin compression as primary reason for cheap valuation.

Trading cheaply at ~9x earnings primarily due to credit risk exposure. While Discover network volume grew 25%, lending remains core business with net charge-off rates as key metric. Economic slowdown could reverse recent credit quality improvements.
